Ravana. The primary antagonist of the Hindu epic Ramayana, a demon king of extraordinary power and intellect whose abduction of Sita precipitates the entire narrative. Though fundamentally evil in his cosmic role, Ravana is portrayed with surprising complexity: a ruler proud of his accomplishments and deeply attached to his family. His defeat by Rama represents the triumph of Dharma, righteousness, over cosmic chaos and demonic chaos.

He is a demon king with ten heads and twenty arms, granting him supernatural strength and near-invincibility in battle, making him one of mythology's most formidable antagonists. He is the ruler of Lanka, a powerful kingdom across the ocean from India, commanding legions of rakshasas, demons, and vast treasures accumulated through conquest. He abducts Sita, the wife of Rama, Vishnu's incarnation, setting in motion the events of the Ramayana and the entire narrative of restoration and heroism.

He is of Brahmin heritage despite his demonic nature. He originally obtained a boon of invulnerability through strict asceticism, making himself vulnerable only to man or monkey, a fatal loophole. A skilled warrior and strategist who commands vast armies and demonstrates considerable intellect, yet ultimately proves no match for Rama supported by divine grace and Hanuman's unfailing loyalty. He is killed by Rama in the climactic battle that restores Dharma and retrieves the stolen Sita, vindicating righteousness over tyranny and chaos.

He is viewed by some traditions with nuance as a figure tragic in his pride, devoted to his family and kingdom, yet ultimately imprisoned by his own ego, sin, and inability to resist temptation. His character demonstrates the Hindu concept that even demons possess intellect and complexity, yet their choices ultimately determine their fate in the cosmic order.

Rama is Vishnu's incarnation and Ravana's arch-nemesis, representing righteousness against demonic chaos. Sita is the abducted wife whose seizure triggers the entire epic narrative. The Ramayana is the Hindu epic whose central plot revolves around Ravana's abduction and defeat. Hanuman is the loyal monkey-devotee of Rama who proves instrumental in Ravana's downfall. Vishnu is the supreme deity whose incarnation as Rama opposes Ravana. Dharma is the cosmic order that Ravana's actions violate and that Rama restores through his victory. Hinduism is the religious tradition that transmits Ravana's story as a moral and spiritual lesson.
